answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to stake a refundable deposit, slashed on proven fraud, and bonded to a verifiable work history. Like a willow that bends yet holds its roots, a real agent builds a reputation echo across many transactions, while a fake starts with none. A nebula of cheap sock-puppets collapses because every new identity must lock fresh funds and earn history from zero, so attacking at scale costs real capital and time.
